matches.rationale: Both identify the same contradiction in the Abstract: the paper claims ALFAR is training-free while also implying training/fine-tuning is involved. Pred_id 1 explicitly quotes the self-contradiction about training-free vs. fine-tuning claims.

GT_id 2 concerns an unusual asymmetric fusion formula in Equation (11) with additive/subtractive scaling terms that can produce negative weights. Pred_id 6 discusses a different issue: that λ_v^t + λ_c^t < 1 (weights don't sum to 1), not the asymmetric formula structure. These are distinct mathematical issues.

Both identify the same experimental bias: ALFAR uses four GPUs while baselines use only one GPU, creating an unfair comparison. Pred_id 7 explicitly states this asymmetric compute allocation undermines fairness.

Both concern inflated accuracy numbers in Tables 2 and 3. GT_id 4 states ALFAR numbers are boosted 3-5% beyond original results; pred_id 2 quotes Table 2's caption stating 'gains reduced by 3-5%' and 'less dramatic than claimed,' identifying the same data integrity issue.

Both address exaggerated claims about ALFAR 'fully exploiting' retrieved knowledge. Pred_id 5 shows Figure 1's ground-truth knowledge yields no improvement (39.15 = parametric score), contradicting the 'fully exploits' claim mentioned in the caption and discussion.
GT_id 6 concerns missing IRB approvals, consent procedures, and privacy safeguards in the Appendix acknowledgments. None of the findings mention ethical review, IRB, consent, or privacy omissions.

GT_id 7 concerns references citing papers from 2025 or later (beyond knowledge cutoff) or imaginary authors/venues, e.g., reference [12]. Pred_id 4 concerns reference [71] (GPT-4) being mislabeled as unpublished when it's actually on arXiv—a different reference and different type of error.

GT_id 8 concerns promotional rhetoric in the Introduction ('fully exploits,' 'superior performance by large margins') without caveats. While pred_id 2 and 5 touch on exaggerated claims, they focus on data inconsistencies in tables/figures, not the rhetorical tone of the Introduction text itself.

Both identify contradictory performance numbers for ALFAR in Figure 1 vs. text. GT_id 9 notes text reports higher numbers than the figure shows; pred_id 5 documents specific numerical conflicts between Figure 1 and Tables 3/A3 for the same dataset.

Both concern unfair experimental comparisons due to heterogeneous baselines and unnormalized conditions. GT_id 10 mentions mixing different model sizes/architectures without normalization; pred_id 7 identifies the specific GPU allocation asymmetry (4 vs. 1 GPU) as undermining fair comparison.

Both identify the contradiction between Section 6.3 (claiming scalability issues and performance decline on InstructBLIP 13B) and Section 6.5/Table 8 (showing large gains on InstructBLIP 13B). Pred_id 3 explicitly documents this cross-section inconsistency.

GT_id 12 concerns missing bias evaluations and safety analyses for knowledge bases in the experimental setup. None of the findings mention bias evaluation, safety analysis, or ethical concerns about knowledge base content.

Both concern misattribution of the GPT-4 technical report in reference [71]. GT_id 13 states it's incorrectly cited as arXiv preprint rather than OpenAI internal; pred_id 4 states it's mislabeled as 'Unpublished internal document' when it's actually a published arXiv preprint—same underlying issue.

GT_id 14 concerns selective rhetoric in the Conclusion omitting limitations (dependency on retrieval, compute cost, scalability). None of the findings specifically address omissions or rhetorical manipulation in the Conclusion section.

GT_id 15 concerns selective citation in Related Work that neglects recent training-free fusion techniques, biasing novelty claims. None of the findings mention citation bias, selective literature review, or omissions in the Related Work section.

Both concern missing or incomplete attention reallocation formulas in Section 4.1. GT_id 16 notes formulas don't ensure causal mask preservation; pred_id 8 identifies that Equation 5 is missing entirely and the image-token adjustment mechanism is unspecified—same underlying gap in method specification.
